result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B gives a clearer rule for covering the whole site: bulk decisions with a 10% spot-check, close reading of the top pages by traffic, branch pages and policy pages, and a calibrated first pass by the helper. Its director deliverable is also stronger, with ranked recommendations, effort estimates and a note on what was left out. A is tighter and its focus on owners and upkeep is good, but its sampling rule is vague ('everything else: read it') and it assumes 11 hand-built layouts. Both answers run over the word limit, B by more. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer A gives a clearer rule for what gets read closely and what gets sampled: decide the obvious groups in bulk and spot-check about 10% of each, then read the high-traffic, branch and service pages one by one. Its director package is also more actionable, with ranked recommendations, effort estimates, a note on what wasn't covered and a 90-day plan. Answer B is strong on ownership and on checking facts with branch managers, but its sampling rule is vaguer ('everything else: read it'). It also adds doing the deletions to week 6. Both answers run past 700 words.
